title: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013
summary: South Africa's general data-protection law, which sets conditions for lawful processing of personal information by public and private bodies and establishes the Information Regulator. Section 71 restricts decisions with legal or substantial effects on a person that rest solely on automated processing used to profile them, for example on work performance, creditworthiness, health or conduct. Exceptions apply for contracts and where a law or code of conduct provides safeguards; those safeguards must let the person make representations and receive information about the logic of the processing. Most provisions, including section 71, took effect on 1 July 2020.
key_obligations: Process personal information only under the Act's conditions for lawful processing
No solely automated profiling decisions with legal or substantial effect, unless an exception applies
Let affected persons make representations on automated decisions
Explain the underlying logic of automated processing to affected persons
